changes.new: Let O be the coefficient discrete valuation ring with uniformizer pi. Write eta for the prescribed continuous central character on compact modules. Let R be the quotient of O[[K]] by the closed ideal generated by z-eta(z) for z in the central compact subgroup. In the BM application, eta=zeta_BM^(-1), because C(O) consists of Pontryagin duals of smooth representations with central character zeta_BM. This compact character is distinct from the smooth-side zeta notation in Section 1.

changes.new: In BM Theorem 5.2, M is Coker(x). The displayed snake-lemma argument there proves O-torsion-freeness; its reduction is the dual of the K-injective envelope, hence the projective envelope of the finite K-socle dual. This reduction is finite projective, not just an unspecified projective object. Indeed, lift finitely many generators of its finite semisimple target to the projective cover Pbar. The image of the resulting continuous map (R/pi R)^n to Pbar is compact, hence closed, and surjects onto that target. Essentiality of the cover makes this image all of Pbar. The surjection splits by projectivity, so Pbar is a finite projective R/pi R-module.
